[[File:Brian Hunter FreedomCon 2001.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Brian Hunter at FreedomCon 2001.]]
'''Brian Hunter''' (GPN / DeckTech handle '''HuntaWarya''')<ref name="dt-23598">[http://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/23598 Saber Combat done RIGHT aka No Mans Land], DeckTech (Brian "HuntaWarya" Hunter, 26 May 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009132707/http://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/23598/ Internet Archive]</ref> won the [[2002 Vegas DPC]] 5–0 with a [[Light]] [[Plead My Case To The Senate / Sanity And Compassion|Plead My Case To The Senate]] list (''LS Senate done RIGHT aka Ghhhks Away'').<ref name="dt-23407">[http://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/23407 LS Senate done RIGHT aka Ghhhks Away], DeckTech (Brian "HuntaWarya" Hunter, 18 May 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009181430/http://www.decktech.net/starwarsccg/deck/23407/ Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="dpc-vegas-tr">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2002-05-15-vegas-baby-lush-at-the-vegas-dpcd3660/ vegas-baby-lush-at-the-vegas-dpc], Matt "Old Skooler" Lush, DeckTech (15 May 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009181430/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2002-05-15-vegas-baby-lush-at-the-vegas-dpcd3660/ Internet Archive]</ref> He won the [[2002 Houston DPC]].<ref name="dpc-houston-tr">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2002-07-16-houston-texas-07-14-02-dpc-houstond3841/ houston-texas-07-14-02-dpc-houston], Jacob "Armaedes" Taylor, DeckTech (16 July 2002). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009144852/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2002-07-16-houston-texas-07-14-02-dpc-houstond3841/ Internet Archive]</ref> He finished 2nd at the [[2006 World Championship]] in Chicago, losing to [[Nate Meeker]].<ref name="awards">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Awards and Hall of Fame], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20230817222457/https://www.starwarsccg.org/community/awards/ Internet Archive] (17 August 2023); [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016161923/https://swccg.com/snapshots/pc/community-awards.html Internet Archive] (snapshot, 16 October 2026)</ref> He finished 4th at the [[2001 Decipher World Championship]].<ref name="fc-home">[http://decktech.net/freedomcon/ FreedomCon home page], decktech.net. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20011201221615/http://decktech.net/freedomcon/ Internet Archive, 1 December 2001]</ref>

== 2007 World Championship interview ==

At the [[2007 World Championship]], his sixth Worlds, Hunter said he first attended Worlds in 2001. He said he did not travel to major events until 2000 and considered 1997–1999 his peak. He qualified for 2007 by winning West Nationals.<ref name="hunter07">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=swSmLNAG62A&t=783s Worlds 2007 P Johnson Interview], Star Wars CCG, YouTube (uploaded 7 April 2026), at 13:03. Transcript: [[2007 World Championship interviews (transcript)]]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015174617/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=swSmLNAG62A Internet Archive]</ref> Before Wizards of the Coast released its ''Star Wars'' trading card game, the company flew six Decipher SWCCG players to Seattle to see it. Hunter won the first Wizards tournament he entered and played in that game's first world championship, but preferred to keep playing SWCCG.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=swSmLNAG62A&t=1180s Worlds 2007 P Johnson Interview], Star Wars CCG, YouTube (uploaded 7 April 2026), at 19:40. Transcript: [[2007 World Championship interviews (transcript)]]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015174617/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=swSmLNAG62A Internet Archive]</ref>
